# Everyday and preventive counselling {#sec-cases}

The four cases below are encounters with a **simulated patient**, someone who plays the patient in a
practice consultation (here, an AI model). Whereas the cases in earlier chapters drill one idea at a time
through set choices, here you talk with the patient in your own words, then get feedback on your
counselling. Each encounter draws together the nutrition science, communication, and clinical
reasoning built up across the book.

All four patients are typical of everyday preventive care. They feel well, or nearly well, and need a
brief history, a misconception gently addressed, and a single realistic change they will actually
make.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The patient is an **AI simulation for practice, not a real person, and not medical advice**.
Treat it as a natural consultation: ask, listen, and agree a realistic plan. If the simulated
patient is unavailable, the encounter notes this and continues.
:::

## Mdm Tan: newly detected prediabetes

A 52-year-old primary-school teacher whose screening blood test showed a raised fasting glucose.
Take a brief diet history, agree one realistic change with her, and check her confidence.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-prediabetes-mdm-tan.case.yml"></div>

## Mr Lim: everyday nutrition questions

A 41-year-old taxi driver whose health screen flagged a borderline fasting glucose and mildly raised
cholesterol. He feels well but has a string of nutrition questions picked up from friends and
online. Answer them by focusing on overall diet quality rather than banning foods, and notice when a plan needs a dietitian.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-common-questions-mr-lim.case.yml"></div>

## Mr Tan: lifestyle beyond diet at a health screen

A 38-year-old software engineer in for a pre-employment screen. He is asymptomatic and sceptical
that anything is wrong. Engage him without lecturing, look beyond his diet, and see if you can agree
one realistic change.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-pillar-mr-tan.case.yml"></div>

## Mdm Goh: fear of dementia

A 55-year-old secondary-school teacher whose mother has dementia. She has a bag of brain
supplements and dismisses her slightly raised blood pressure and borderline glucose. Take her fear
seriously, then lead with what actually lowers the risk.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-dementia-prevention-mdm-goh.case.yml"></div>
